description: An interest-bearing deposit account for everyday saving, with funds generally available on demand through the bank's supported channels.
similarity_notes: Both hold liquid personal savings and may pay interest while allowing withdrawals.
difference_notes: Fees, minimum balances, access channels, and interest calculations are bank-specific in both countries; compare the actual account disclosures.

sources.title: Dhaka Bank deposit rates and product categories

description: A transaction-focused demand deposit account used for frequent deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and business payments.
similarity_notes: Both are transaction accounts intended for routine payments and on-demand access.
difference_notes: The term 'current account' commonly means a transaction account in Bangladesh, while US banks normally call that product a checking account.

sources.title: Dhaka Bank deposit rates and product categories

description: A lump-sum bank deposit held until a stated maturity date, usually in exchange for a higher return than an ordinary savings account.
similarity_notes: Both place a lump sum in a bank for a defined term and may impose a cost for taking money out early.
difference_notes: Product disclosures, renewal rules, taxation, and deposit-insurance coverage differ; a US CD is not legally identical to an FDR.

sources.title: CFPB definition of certificate of deposit

description: A goal-based deposit plan funded with a fixed installment each month for an agreed period.
closest_us_equivalent: Goal-based recurring savings (no direct standard US equivalent)
similarity_notes: The nearest US behavior is an automatic monthly transfer into a goal-based savings account.
difference_notes: A DPS is a packaged contractual deposit scheme; automatic transfers to a normal US savings account generally do not create the same fixed installment and maturity contract.

description: A term deposit funded with a lump sum that distributes earnings periodically during the term.
similarity_notes: The principal is committed for a term, like a CD; some US CDs also distribute interest periodically.
difference_notes: Payout schedules, early-withdrawal treatment, and renewal terms depend on the specific institution and are not implied by the mapping.

sources.title: Dhaka Bank Special Deposit Scheme description

description: A bank account for day-to-day surplus funds that permits withdrawals and commonly provides digital banking and debit-card access.
similarity_notes: Both are liquid deposit accounts primarily used to hold personal savings.
difference_notes: Withdrawal rules, minimum balances, payment features, and interest methods vary by institution; compare the individual product terms.

sources.title: RBI financial education guide on deposit types

description: A demand deposit account designed for frequent payments and withdrawals, commonly used for business activity.
similarity_notes: Both are designed to move money and make routine payments rather than lock savings for a term.
difference_notes: Indian banks use 'current account' where US consumer banks usually use 'checking account'; eligibility and fees remain institution-specific.

description: A lump-sum deposit placed with a bank for a chosen fixed period, normally with reduced earnings if withdrawn before maturity.
similarity_notes: Both use a lump-sum deposit, a stated term, and an early-withdrawal consequence.
difference_notes: Tax reporting, automatic renewal, insurance, and premature-withdrawal rules differ between institutions and countries.

description: A deposit plan that builds savings through a fixed amount paid at regular intervals for a set period.
closest_us_equivalent: Goal-based recurring savings (no direct standard US equivalent)
similarity_notes: The nearest common US practice is scheduling automatic transfers into a savings goal.
difference_notes: An Indian RD is a defined deposit product with installment and maturity terms; an ordinary US automatic savings plan is usually just a transfer instruction.

sources.title: RBI financial education guide on recurring deposits

description: A basic, KYC-compliant savings account intended to provide essential deposit and payment services without a minimum-balance requirement.
similarity_notes: The nearest US comparison is a certified low-cost or checkless account designed around essential transactions and transparent fees.
difference_notes: BSBDA is an RBI-defined Indian account category; the US comparison is a functional analogy, not the same regulatory product.

sources.title: SBI Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account

description: An interest-bearing deposit account with funds withdrawable on demand through supported bank channels such as a passbook, ATM, or online banking.
similarity_notes: Both keep personal savings liquid and may earn interest.
difference_notes: Maintaining-balance rules, access methods, and fees vary by product and may differ from common US savings accounts.

sources.title: BSP Financial Reporting Package deposit definitions

description: A transaction deposit account subject to withdrawal by check and other available banking channels.
similarity_notes: Both are transaction accounts supporting checks and routine payments.
difference_notes: Account-opening minimums, check practices, fees, and interest treatment depend on the specific bank product.

sources.title: BSP Financial Reporting Package deposit definitions

description: An interest-bearing lump-sum deposit with a specified maturity date.
similarity_notes: Both hold a lump sum until a specified maturity and commonly limit early access.
difference_notes: Withholding tax, insurance, rates, documentation, and early-withdrawal rules differ; review the specific disclosures.

sources.title: BSP Financial Reporting Package deposit definitions

description: A simplified deposit account designed for financial inclusion, with easy opening, no maintaining balance, and a capped balance under BSP rules.
similarity_notes: Both focus on affordable access to core deposit and payment services.
difference_notes: The Philippine BDA has BSP-defined features and limits; US low-cost accounts use different standards and do not reproduce the BDA rules.

sources.title: BSP Manual of Regulations for Banks — Basic Deposit Account

description: An interest-bearing deposit account from which funds can be withdrawn using negotiable orders of withdrawal.
similarity_notes: Both combine transaction access with the possibility of earning interest.
difference_notes: The legal form, permitted instruments, eligibility, rates, and fees are governed by different national rules.

description: A deposit account used to hold accessible savings and potentially earn interest.
A demand deposit account used for everyday transactions such as debit-card purchases, checks, transfers, and bill payments.
A special type of savings account in which funds generally remain for a specified period to avoid an early-withdrawal penalty.
